summary: @apexfdn/apex postinstall drops executable from unrelated GitHub org and runs it as the CLI
details: On npm install, the package's postinstall script fetches a platform-specific binary from github.com/Apex-Foundation/copilot releases (URL constructed as https://github.com/Apex-Foundation/copilot/releases/download/v${RELEASE_VERSION}/${assetName}) and writes it to bin/apex(.exe) with mode 0755. No hash or signature verification is performed; the downloaded bytes become the entire implementation of the CLI. The bin wrapper apex.cjs then subprocess-execs that binary with the user's argv and full process.env. Publisher metadata is inconsistent with the binary source: package.json declares author 'Can Boluk', repository can1357/oh-my-pi, and homepage omp.sh, and the README is verbatim documentation for @oh-my-pi/pi-coding-agent, but the fetched executable comes from an unrelated 'Apex-Foundation/copilot' GitHub org. The declared main./src/index.ts is not shipped in the tarball, so the package has no first-party runtime code — the fetched opaque binary is the entire runtime surface. Whoever controls the Apex-Foundation/copilot releases can execute arbitrary code on installer machines when the apex CLI is invoked.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
